## Notes

### Quick read
- Michelle is a cheerful mom of five (baby girl about 6 months in August, plus a 4-year-old boy and older kids) with a playful, funny voiceover style; both her videos ran as 2 ads each but she has not uploaded since Aug 7.
- Best next move: send the 10 weekly video ideas Fatima promised on Sep 22 (still owed), and make sure they keep one hand on baby, since her kitchen video shows both hands busy.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- Who she is on camera: mom of five, long light brown hair, glasses in one video, casual tees and jeans, barefoot at home, friendly and a bit goofy. Baby girl (number 5, a "stage 5 Velcro baby", 6 months per the Aug 6 script) and a blond 4-year-old boy who loves riding in the sling. Settings: a family kitchen with granite counters and kids' art on the fridge, and a playroom with a painted rainbow and sun mural and gym rings. Slings: Checkered and a colourful mandala strap.
- Format: voiceover with bold caption text, light humour, 15 to 22s, quick cuts. Shows real life tasks (making a PB and J while wearing baby) and a comedic toddler ride.
- Hooks (quote): "Being a mom of 5 is already a juggling act, but when baby number 5 is a stage 5 Velcro baby, putting her down is simply not an option."; "I fully intended to get the Bambora Sling for my 6-month-old, but then my 4-year-old realized I would willingly carry him in it... Sir, you have legs!"
- What worked: both approved and both running as 2 ads each (6eb47f7d mom of 5 kitchen, e1f63d73 4-year-old rides). $1,003 ad spend but only $97 Trybe GMV and ROAS 1.03, so good spend, middling conversion. Both use "save your arms", our approved relief angle.
- Safety and checklist issues seen:
  - 6eb47f7d (running as 2 ads): while making a sandwich both hands are on the bread bag and jam jar at 11s, 15s and 19s, with no hand on the baby. This breaks check 2 (one hand at all times) and is the kind of shot other parents copy. Worth flagging to the media buyer.
  - e1f63d73 (running): 4-year-old in the sling; her arm stays around him. Fine if he is under 50 lbs; seat looks under his bottom.
  - Baby's seat in the kitchen video is under the bottom with legs out; M position not really visible.
- Strengths to lean on: humour and relatable big family chaos; real kids who are happy on camera; strong arm-relief messaging.
- To improve: one hand on baby even while cooking (or film the task with baby but hand on); more volume.
